title: Move along or shift?

predict.q: A specialist parts supplier opens next to a cluster of bike makers, cutting each maker's costs. One maker's output stays the same. What happens on its LRAC diagram?

options.s: It moves down along its LRAC curve
options.fb: Moving along the curve needs a change in the firm's own output. Here output is fixed and costs fall at every output: a shift.
External economies cut cost at every output, so the whole curve shifts down to LRAC2, even though this firm's output is unchanged.
An upward shift would mean costs rise, e.g. from congestion. A nearby supplier lowers costs.

options.s: Nothing, because its own output has not changed
options.fb: External economies change cost at every output, so the curve moves even when this firm's output does not.

task: Move the **firm output** slider: the point slides along LRAC1. Then move the **industry size** slider: the whole curve shifts down to LRAC2.

target.do: Move the industry size slider up from 3 (to 4, 5 or 6), then press Check.

takeaway: The firm's own growth moves it **along** the curve (internal); the industry's growth **shifts** the curve (external).
